SECTION B — Short Answer Questions - I (2 Marks Each)

Q5. State why a magnesium ribbon should be cleaned with sandpaper before burning in air. Write the balanced chemical equation with state symbols.

Model Answer: Magnesium metal is reactive and forms a protective, unreactive layer of magnesium oxide upon storage in air. Rubbing with sandpaper removes this coating so the clean metal is directly exposed to atmospheric oxygen for ignition.
2Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2MgO(s) + Light + Heat

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 marks — (1 mark for reason of removing oxide layer + 1 mark for balanced equation with state symbols).

Q6. What colour change is observed when green ferrous sulphate crystals are heated strongly in a dry boiling tube? Name the gases evolved.

Model Answer:
  • Colour Change: Green crystals turn into a reddish-brown solid (ferric oxide, Fe2O3).
  • Gases Evolved: Pungent gases with the odour of burning sulphur: sulphur dioxide (SO2) and sulphur trioxide (SO3).

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 marks — (1 mark for colour change pale green → reddish-brown + 1 mark for naming SO2 and SO3).

SECTION C — Short Answer Questions - II (3 Marks Each)

Q7. Explain the hit-and-trial method for balancing the skeletal equation Fe + H2O → Fe3O4 + H2 by showing the inventory of atoms for each step.

Model Working:
1. Balance Oxygen: 4 O atoms in Fe3O4 (RHS) → Multiply H2O by 4 on LHS: Fe + 4H2O → Fe3O4 + H2.
2. Balance Hydrogen: LHS has 8 H atoms → Multiply H2 by 4 on RHS: Fe + 4H2O → Fe3O4 + 4H2.
3. Balance Iron & Add States: RHS has 3 Fe → Multiply Fe by 3 on LHS: 3Fe(s) + 4H2O(g) → Fe3O4(s) + 4H2(g).

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 marks — (1 mark for balancing O + 1 mark for balancing H + 1 mark for balancing Fe with state symbols).

Q8. Write one balanced chemical equation each for decomposition reactions triggered by: (a) Heat, (b) Light, and (c) Electricity.

Model Answer:
  • (a) Heat: CaCO3(s) Heat
    →     CaO(s) + CO2(g)
  • (b) Light: 2AgCl(s) Sunlight
    →     2Ag(s) + Cl2(g)
  • (c) Electricity: 2H2O(l) Electricity
    →     2H2(g) + O2(g)

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 marks — (1 mark for each correctly balanced equation with condition indicated).

SECTION D — Case-Based Practical Question (6 Marks Total: 4 + 2)

Q9. Case Study on Electrolysis of Water: During an experiment on electrolysis of acidified water in a laboratory apparatus (Fig. 1.6), a student observed continuous gas evolution at both carbon electrodes.
(i) Name the gas collected at the cathode and the anode. (1 Mark)
(ii) Why is the volume of gas collected at one electrode double that at the other? (2 Marks)
(iii) Why are a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid added to water? (1 Mark)
(iv) How can the gases evolved be experimentally identified? (2 Marks)

Model Answer:
(i) Gas Identities: Cathode (−) = Hydrogen (H2); Anode (+) = Oxygen (O2).
(ii) 2:1 Volume Reason: A water molecule is composed of 2 atoms of hydrogen and 1 atom of oxygen. During electrolysis, 2 volumes of H2 are liberated for every 1 volume of O2: 2H2O → 2H2 + O2.
(iii) Role of Acid: Pure water is poorly ionised; acid provides mobile ions (H+, SO42−) to conduct electricity.
(iv) Confirmatory Tests: Hydrogen burns with a 'pop' sound when tested with a burning candle. Oxygen rekindles a glowing splint / causes a flame to burn brighter.

📌 Marking Scheme: 6 marks — (1M for gas names + 2M for 2:1 ratio explanation + 1M for acid conductivity + 2M for candle tests).

📝 CBSE Practice Test 2 — Displacement, Double Displacement, Redox & Corrosion/Rancidity (Max Marks: 20) ▼

⏳ Time Allowed: 45 Minutes  |  📊 Maximum Marks: 20 Marks

📌 General Instructions: All questions are compulsory. Marks are indicated against each question.

SECTION A — Multiple Choice & Objective Questions (1 Mark Each)

Q1. When an iron nail is immersed in copper sulphate solution for 20 minutes, the colour of the solution turns:

  1. Colourless
  2. Deep blue
  3. Pale green
  4. Yellowish brown
Answer: (C) Pale green, due to the formation of ferrous sulphate (FeSO4).

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 mark

Q2. In the reaction MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2, the substance that is oxidised is:

  1. MnO2
  2. HCl
  3. MnCl2
  4. Cl2
Answer: (B) HCl. It loses hydrogen atoms to form Cl2 (oxidation).

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 mark

Q3. Assertion (A): Chips packets are flushed with nitrogen gas before packaging.
Reason (R): Nitrogen is an antioxidant and acts as a chemically inert blanket preventing atmospheric oxidation of oils.

  1. Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
  2. Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
  3. A is true, but R is false
  4. A is false, but R is true
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and R correctly explains why nitrogen prevents rancidity in fried snacks.

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 mark

Q4. The green coating formed on copper upon exposure to air is chemically:

  1. CuSO4
  2. CuO
  3. CuCO3·Cu(OH)2
  4. CuCl2
Answer: (C) Basic copper carbonate [CuCO3·Cu(OH)2].

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 mark

SECTION B — Short Answer Questions - I (2 Marks Each)

Q5. What is a precipitation reaction? Provide a balanced chemical equation with state symbols.

Model Answer: Any chemical reaction occurring in aqueous medium that results in the formation of an insoluble solid substance (precipitate) is called a precipitation reaction.
Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) → BaSO4(s)↓ [White precipitate] + 2NaCl(aq)

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 marks — (1 mark for definition of insoluble precipitate + 1 mark for balanced equation with state symbols).

Q6. State two practical methods to prevent rancidity in fat- and oil-containing food items.

Model Answer:
  1. Adding Antioxidants: Adding substances such as BHA or BHT to retard oxidation.
  2. Flushing with Nitrogen Gas: Packaging snacks in bags flushed with unreactive nitrogen gas to exclude oxygen.

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 marks — (1 mark for each valid prevention method).

SECTION C — Short Answer Questions - II (3 Marks Each)

Q7. Distinguish between displacement and double displacement reactions by providing: (i) Definition, (ii) One balanced equation for each, and (iii) One observable difference.

Model Answer:
Displacement: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its aqueous salt solution.
Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)
Double Displacement: Two ionic compounds mutually exchange their ions to form two new compounds.
BaCl2(aq) + Na2SO4(aq) → BaSO4(s)↓ + 2NaCl(aq)
Observable Difference: Displacement involves a colour change and solid metal deposition; double displacement typically results in an immediate insoluble precipitate.

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 marks — (1M for definitions + 1M for equations + 1M for observable difference).

Q8. Identify the: (a) Substance oxidised, (b) Substance reduced, (c) Oxidising agent, and (d) Reducing agent in: CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O.

Model Answer:
  • (a) Substance Oxidised: H2 (gains oxygen to form H2O).
  • (b) Substance Reduced: CuO (loses oxygen to form Cu).
  • (c) Oxidising Agent: CuO (provides oxygen for oxidation).
  • (d) Reducing Agent: H2 (removes oxygen from CuO).

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 marks — (1 mark for oxidised/reduced + 2 marks for oxidising/reducing agents).

SECTION D — Long Answer / HOTS Question (6 Marks Total: 3 + 3)

Q9. Comprehensive Analytical Problem:
(a) A reddish-brown metal 'P' on heating in air forms a black compound 'Q'. When hydrogen gas is passed over heated 'Q', 'P' is regenerated. Identify 'P' and 'Q' and write both chemical equations. (3 Marks)
(b) What is corrosion? Name the colour of the coating developed by iron, silver, and copper during corrosion, and write one method to prevent corrosion of iron. (3 Marks)

Model Answer:
Part (a): Identification of P and Q:
'P' = Copper metal [Cu]
'Q' = Copper(II) oxide [CuO]
Reaction 1 (Oxidation): 2Cu(s) + O2(g) Heat
→ 2CuO(s) [Black]
Reaction 2 (Reduction): CuO(s) + H2(g) Heat
→ Cu(s) [Brown] + H2O(g)
Part (b): Corrosion Analysis:
Definition: The slow chemical eating away of a metal by atmospheric moisture, oxygen, and acidic gases.
Coatings:
  • Iron: Reddish-brown flaky rust [Fe2O3·xH2O]
  • Silver: Black tarnish [Ag2S]
  • Copper: Green patina [CuCO3·Cu(OH)2]
Prevention of Iron Rusting: Painting / Galvanisation (coating with zinc) / Greasing to isolate iron from air and moisture.

📌 Marking Scheme: 6 marks — (Part (a): 1.5M for P & Q + 1.5M for two equations; Part (b): 1M for definition + 1.5M for three coatings + 0.5M for prevention method).

🚀 8. Rapid Revision (10 Key Takeaways) & Chemical Reaction Reference Sheet
⚡

10 Rapid Revision Key Takeaways — Flash Cards

  • 1. Chemical Change Indicators: A chemical reaction is signaled by (i) change in state, (ii) change in colour, (iii) evolution of gas, or (iv) change in temperature.
  • 2. Balancing Rule: Every chemical equation must be balanced to satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass (total mass and atom counts on LHS = RHS).
  • 3. Combination Reaction (A + B → AB): Two or more reactants join to form a single product. Example: CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq) + Heat.
  • 4. Decomposition Reaction (AB → A + B): A single compound splits into simpler components upon absorption of heat (thermal), light (photochemical), or electricity (electrolytic).
  • 5. Exothermic vs Endothermic: Exothermic reactions evolve heat (respiration, combustion of methane, quick lime hydration). Endothermic reactions absorb energy (all decompositions, barium hydroxide + ammonium chloride).
  • 6. Single Displacement (A + BC → AC + B): A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution (e.g. Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu).
  • 7. Double Displacement (AB + CD → AD + CB): Two ionic compounds mutually exchange ions. Often forms an insoluble precipitate (e.g. Na2SO4 + BaCl2 → BaSO4↓ + 2NaCl).
  • 8. Redox Integrated Process: Oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen. Reduction = loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen. Both occur simultaneously in a redox reaction.
  • 9. Corrosion: Atmospheric deterioration of metals: Iron forms reddish-brown rust (Fe2O3·xH2O); Silver turns black (Ag2S); Copper turns green [CuCO3·Cu(OH)2].
  • 10. Rancidity Prevention: Fats/oils oxidise to cause bad taste and smell. Prevented by antioxidants, nitrogen flushing, vacuum sealing, and low temperatures.
🧠

High-Yield Memory Hooks

🧠 Memory Hook 1 (Redox): OIL RIG — Oxidation Is Loss (of electrons/hydrogen; gain of oxygen) • Reduction Is Gain (of electrons/hydrogen; loss of oxygen).
🧠 Memory Hook 2 (The Lime Cycle Triad):
Quick Lime (CaO, dry solid) +H2O
→ Slaked Lime [Ca(OH)2, aqueous solution] +CO2
→ Limestone / Marble (CaCO3, stone hard shiny wall).
🧠 Memory Hook 3 (Metal Reactivity Order):
Zn > Fe > Pb > Cu — "Zebras In Lead Cages" (Zinc displaces Iron, Iron displaces Lead, Lead displaces Copper).
